summary: Market sentiment is cautiously mixed, with U.S. stocks closing lower as investors weigh Middle East tensions against a more constructive earnings backdrop, while European shares extended record highs buoyed by optimism around a potential U.S.-Iran resolution and solid corporate results. The dominant macro driver remains the Iran conflict, with Trump signaling the war could end "pretty soon," yet contradictory signals persist as Saudi Arabia warns of imminent attacks from multiple fronts, Iran's parliament reviews a bill to bar U.S. and Israeli ships from the Strait of Hormuz, and shipping industry sources call any Hormuz passage deal unfeasible. In sector and stock news, gold steadied while oil rose on Hormuz supply risk; ConocoPhillips flagged limited delays to Qatar LNG projects; Sweetgreen slashed its full-year outlook on cyclospora outbreak fears; easyJet agreed to a $7.7 billion Apollo takeover; and American Airlines announced it will end elite coach-to-business upgrades on long domestic routes, signaling margin-focused restructuring in travel. The primary risk factors investors are monitoring include a potential Hormuz closure that could severely disrupt global oil flows, an unresolved and escalating Middle East conflict with no clear exit strategy for the U.S., and mounting geopolitical flashpoints including Syrian instability and new U.S. sanctions on Cuban military entities. In the short term, markets are likely to remain volatile and headline-driven, with energy and defense sectors outperforming, while consumer-facing names and rate-sensitive assets face pressure until clearer resolution emerges on the Iran situation and earnings season provides more directional guidance.
